body: Linear probes recover character properties of a word from a language model's hidden states, but a probe at the answer position cannot say whether the property was stored with the word or produced because the prompt asked for it. We separate the two with a word-position baseline: the same held-out-word probe applied to the query word's own tokens in a sentence that asks nothing. Across 16 open-weight models from seven families (0.6B--14B) and eleven character tasks, the word tokens encode first_letter, last_letter and most_frequent_letter above a word-only nuisance floor in all 16 models, and about 70% of that signal is already present in the token embedding. Asking the question adds a second signal at the answer position. Its size grows with model scale for all four prompt-sensitive tasks (Holm-corrected permutation p ≤ 0.018, also within model families), and the growth is confined to the late layers: restricted to the first quarter of the network, the slope is indistinguishable from zero. Small models' answer positions hold less linearly decodable signal than their word-level store; large models' hold more. Four controls bound these claims. Measured against the nuisance floor, the question-free signal that a majority-baseline analysis counts as retained largely disappears (last_letter: -0.01). Count tasks become measurable only after length, repetition and query-letter shortcuts are removed by design. A pre-registered test finds that a question placed before the word does not change the word's own encoding beyond what an arbitrary prefix change does. Representation--readout gaps show no robust scaling once probe saturation is accounted for. Pre-registered criteria, a fixed estimator (held-out layer selection, cold-start folds) and all analysis code accompany the paper.
summaryZh: 语言模型中的字符信息：独立于提示的单词存储和随规模增长的后期问题驱动信号。线性探针从语言模型的隐藏状态中恢复单词的字符属性，但答案位置的探针无法确定该属性是与单词一起存储还是因为提示要求而产生。我们用单词位置基线将两者分开：在不询问任何内容的句子中，将相同的保留单词探针应用于查询单词自己的标记。
